messages:
dmitri: heads up — after today's release (6f2a9b3) we see a decode p95 spike on shortseq traffic. correlates with the prefetch/batcher change.
ci-bot: CI perf alert: decode_p95 increased ~18% on nightlies for short seqs. dashboard: https://perf.redwood.ai/runs/10723
kevin: seeing same in prod dashboards. p95 up on ~64/128 token calls. flamegraph points to attn_transpose + matmul_fused.
sarah: can you paste the profiler snapshot and any cache stats? wondering if KV cache hit-rate changed.
dmitri: quick profiler snippet below — also saw prefix cache hit-rate drop after rollout (98% -> 74%). suspect prefetch interacts with small batches and serializes work.
```
perf sample (shortseq workload):
attn_transpose 42%
matmul_fused 28%
kv_prefetch_lock 12%
other 18%
```
ajay: ah — we introduced a global prefetch latch in 6f2a9b3 to prevent double-prefetch races. on paper it avoids duplicates, but on small batches that global latch can serialize microbatches.
dmitri: repro command I used: `./bench --model r-llama-7b --seq 64 --batches 1000 --batcher.max=8 --batcher.min=1 --prefetch=true` — reproduces the p95 tail reliably.
kevin: option: revert the latch change or switch to per-shard locks. oncall, can we spin a small canary for a revert? @oncall-bot
oncall-bot: Canary request created — canary: 3 nodes (us-west-2), traffic split: 1%. ID: canary-3996.
sarah: i'll start a bisect on the release branch now to confirm exact commit boundaries. revert candidate is PR #4021 (prefetch: remove global latch).
dmitri: short-term workaround: disable prefetch for shortseq route or bump min_batch to 2. pushing a canary revert now to test impact.
kevin: :thumbsup: keep updates in this thread.
